explanation: The paste is made from dried, powdered henna leaves. It stains the skin orange to deep reddish-brown, and the design fades over a week or two as the skin renews itself.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Henna stains usually last about one to four weeks, though the range is wide. Sources give different figures: one says a few days to a month, another says one to three weeks, and another says one to four weeks.

claimResults.note: Not confirmed as written. The figures found are wider than 'one to two weeks' (one to three or four weeks; palms last longest, face and neck shortest), and the search was mostly low-quality pages. Widen to 'a few weeks' (precision ladder, §9.2).

issues.note: c6: the explanation says the design 'fades over a week or two'. The sources found give one to three or four weeks (hands and feet last longest), so one to two weeks is too narrow. Reword to 'a few weeks' (precision ladder, §9.2). The key and distractors are sound.
